Criminal Appeal No. 59 of 2000
With
Criminal Revision No.  381 of 2001
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Eunus Ali Akond for the complainant- appellant in Criminal Appeal No.59 of 2000 and opposite party No.1 in Criminal Revision No.381 of 2001) 
Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan with Ms. Bulbul Rabeya Banu (For accused-respondent No.1 in Criminal Appeal No.59 of 2000 and the petitioner in Criminal Revision No.381 of 2001) 
Mr. Sk. Rezaul Karim, A.A.G. ------- for the State.
parties:
Mohammad Abdul Halim Chowdhury
Vs.
G.M.M. Rahman, Managing Director, Wonder Land Park, Gulshan, 2. The State
And
G.M.M. Rahman, Gazi Fisheries Ltd.
Vs.
Mohammad Abdul Halim Chowdhury
full_judgment:
2. Prosecution case, stated briefly, is that the complainant appellant is the Proprietor of Continental Sea Foods and the accused namely G. M. M. Rahman is the Managing Director of the Gazi Fisheries Limited. The complainant advanced Tk. 14 lacs to the accused with an interest @ 18% but the accused did not return the money on various pretexts and ultimately agreed to repay only the advance taken by him in five installments as mentioned in the complaint and according to arrangement a cheque for Tk.2 lacs representing the first installment was, drawn on the Khulna Branch of Arab Bangladesh Bank in favour of the complainant on 7.4.1996 and it was to be presented for encashment on 7.5.1996. The cheque was returned without payment by the Bank. The complainant informed the accused of the matter and again deposited the cheque for encashment on 18.6.1996 and this time also the cheque was returned without payment on 23.6.1996 whereafter the complainant served a notice through a lawyer for making necessary arrangement for payment of the cheque money but the accused did not take any step in that regard. Thus the appellant filed the complaint before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate who took cognizance against the accused-respondent-petitioner for an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. 

 4. Prosecution examined 4 witnesses in the case. The accused also examined himself only in support of his defence. 

 5. Defence case, as it transpires from the trend of cross-examination as well as the deposition of the accused as D.W.1 is that the transaction between the two companies and as such the accused has no personal liability. The cheque was not dishonoured due to insufficient fund but was merely referred to the drawer. The liability, if any, of the accused is civil liability and the criminal case, in the absence of any ingredient of an offence u/s. 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, is not maintainable. 

 6. The learned Metropolitan Magistrate, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, found the accused-respondent guilty of an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and sentenced him to pay fine of Tk. 4 lacs being double the amount of the cheque. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order of conviction and sentence, the complainant has preferred the instant appeal. The accused-respondent also preferred Metropolitan Appeal Case No. 1583 of 1999 against the impugned order of conviction and sentence before the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka, and the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, dismissed the appeal confirming the order of conviction and sentence dated 14.11.1999 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. The respondent, being aggrieved by the order of the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, has preferred the aforesaid Criminal Revision which has also been heard together with this appeal as common questions of law and facts are involved. 

 10. There is no dispute about the fact that the complainant, the Proprietor of Continental Sea Foods, advanced an amount of Tk. 14 lac to the accused namely G. M. M. Rahman by two cheques being cheque Nos.5890307 dated 4.2.93 and 5890308 dated 9.2.93, both drawn on Arab Bangladesh Bank Limited, Principal Branch, Dhaka and the accused undertook to return back the same with interest @ 18% per annum. It appears from the record that the amount was not returned and ultimately the parties came to an agreement to the effect that the borrower will repay the principal amount in 5 installments and the first installment of Tk. 2 lac was to be paid by 25.4.1996. There is also no dispute that the accused issued the cheque dated 7.4.1996 Exhibit-1, in respect of the 1st installment in favour of the complainant with a request to the complainant to present the cheque on 7.5.96 for encashment. The complainant presented the cheque for collection of the amount on 10.4.96 but the cheque was returned unpaid. The complainant on 15.5.96 issued a notice upon the accused demanding of him the payment of the cheque amount within 30.5.1996. The accused, on receipt of the notice on 17.5.96, did not make any arrangement for payment of the amount. However, the complainant again presented the cheque for encashment on 18.6.96 in the Khulna Branch of Arab Bangladesh Bank but the cheque was again returned unpaid on 23.6.96. Therefore, the complainant filed the case. 

 11. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent of the appeal also being the petitioner of the criminal revision, submits that: (1) the transaction is between the two companies and the accused-respondent was not personally liable to repay the amount and as such the case is misconceived and not tenable in law; (2) No money was due to the complainant from the accused and that the concerned cheque was not dishonoured but merely referred to the drawer; (3) There is no cause of action for the complainant to institute the case and the case has also not been instituted within time and as such it is barred by Sections 138(1) and 141(b) of the Negotiable Instruments Act as the case was not filed within 15 days from the valid cause of action. The learned Advocate in support of his contention has referred to the decisions in the case of S.M. Anwar Hossain -Vs- State reported in 19 BLD (AD) 166; to the case of Abdus Salam Rashed -Vs- State reported in 54 DLR 234 and also to the case of Habibur Rahman-Vs-State reported in 53 DLR (AD) 111; (4) The charge in the case was not properly framed and thereby the accused has been prejudiced and as such the order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside and in support of his contention he has referred to the case of Md. Nizamuddin Dhali-Vs-State reported in 16 BLD 580 and also to the case of Md. Abdul Bari Molla-Vs-State reported in 17 BLD 223 and (5) The incriminating materials were not brought to the notice of the accused during his examination under Section 342 Cr.P.C. by the Magistrate and as such the impugned order of conviction and sentence is to be set aside and the accused-respondent is to be acquitted and in support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred to the decisions reported in 14 BLD 280, 15 BLD 449, 16 BLD 580, 17 BLD 82, 19 BLD 74 and 20 BLD 168. 

 12. Mr. Md. Eunus Ali Akanda, the learned Advocate appearing for the complainant appellant, on the other hand, submits that the money was due from the accused to the appellant and accordingly after much delay the accused agreed to repay only the amount advanced in 5 installments and the cheque for Tk.2 lacs issued for the first installment was drawn on Khulna Branch of the Arab Bangladesh Bank. He issued the concerned cheque for Tk. 2 lacs representing the first installment but the cheque was dishonoured. The complainant then by his letter dated 15.5.1996 asked the accused to make proper arrangement for payment of the money. The accused-respondent having received the same on 17.5.1996 took no step whatsoever for making the fund available and/or for payment the same. The accused committed the offence under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instruments Act and that the case has been filed within one month from the date of cause of action. The learned Advocate also submits that the accused-respondent has not been prejudiced by the framing of charge or by his examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned Advocate further submits that the accused-respondent had due notice of the charge framed against him and evidence adduced against him and he having examined himself as D.W.1 on his behalf tried his best to meet the prosecution case as well as the evidence adduced and as such it cannot be said that the accused-respondent was prejudiced in his defence due any defect in framing the charge against him or due to the strict non-compliance of the provisions of section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned Advocate also submits that in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the conduct of the accused-respondent the learned Metropolitan Magistrate ought to have inflicted maximum punishment on him. 

 15. P.W.1, Abdul Halim Chowdhury is the complainant in this case. He has correctly stated the entire prosecution case and his evidence could not be shaken in the least during cross-examination. 

 19. D.W.1, G. M. M. Rahman is the accused in this case. He says that advancement of money was from Company to Company and that he has no personal liability in the matter. He further says that the cheque was not dishonoured because of insufficient fund. He, however, admits to have issued the cheque and further admits that he issued the cheque as part payment of the advance made by the complainant. He further says that he issued the cheque after amicable settlement regarding return of the advance made by the complainant. 

 20. It is, therefore, apparent that the cheque issued by the accused in favour of the complainant was dishonoured. The cheque was deposited in the concerned account on 18.6.1996 for the second time and it was again dishonoured and referred to the drawer and the cheque was returned on 25.6.1996 to the complainant vide exhibit-3 where after the complainant issued a notice dated 4.7.1996, exhibit-Ka which was received on 7.7.1996 and the accused has also admitted in his deposition to have received the notice but no paper on behalf of the accused could be filed to show that any reply was given. It further transpires from the record that on receipt of the notice by the accused, no arrangement for making payment was made by 22.7.96 by him and as such the complainant filed the case before the Magistrate on 14.8.96 within one month from the date of cause of action and in the three decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the respondent contending that the time for filing a case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is to be calculated from the first date of dishonouring the cheque being 22.7.1996 in the instant case but we are unable to agree with the learned Advocate in this regard because for the second time the cheque was deposited within its currency and the contention of the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent is negatived in the decision reported in 55 DLR 199 referred by the learned Advocate for the respondent himself as well as by the learned Advocate for the appellant wherein it has been held that computation of 15 days for serving notice is to be done from the date on which the cheque was lastly returned by the bank. 

 22. It has been held in the case of Md. Nizamuddin Dhali-Vs-The State reported in 16 BLD 580 that law requires that a charge must contain particulars as to the time and place of the alleged offence, which should reasonably be sufficient to give the accused notice of the matter he is charged with. As it has been held in the case of Md. Abdul Bari Molla-Vs-The State reported in 17 BLD 223 that proviso to section 222(2) of the Code enjoins that the first and last date of the charge of criminal breach of trust or dishonest misappropriation of money shall not exceed one year and in the said case, charge was framed for misappropriation of money between 10.11.1979 and 25.11.1982 that is for a period of over 2 years. Evidently, the trial was held by adopting a mode which is prohibited by law and as such the same was illegal, not curable under Section 537 Cr.P.C. This decision was regarding criminal breach of trust or dishonest misappropriation of money and no misappropriation was made in the case before us. The decisions in the other cases mentioned above also regarding breach of trust and have no manner of application in the case before us in view of the fact of the case but the said decisions lend support to the prosecution case in view of the fact that the accused was given sufficient notice of the nature of the offence and allegations against him. The aforesaid decisions have no manner of application in the case before us and provision of Sub-section (1) of Section 222 of the Code of Criminal Procedure appears to have been sufficiently complied with by the prosecution which is evident from the charge itself as quoted earlier in this judgment. Therefore, the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent with regard to the defective charge does hold good and it cannot be said that the accused could not take any step in the case because of the defect in the charge against him or that he has been prejudiced in his defence in any manner. Moreover, the accused by deposing in this case as D.W.1 also tried to meet the substantive allegations against him and as such it cannot be said that he had no knowledge about it or that he was not aware of the time and place of the alleged offence or of any particular of the offence against him. 

 23. The submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent is that the accused-respondent has also been prejudiced by improper examination under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. There is no denial of the fact that the mandatory provisions of law for examining the accused under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the purpose of enabling him to explain the circumstances appearing in the evidence against him are to be complied with. In the instant case, we are of the view that the accused had sufficient opportunity to explain the incriminating circumstances and he did so in his deposition during examination and cross-examination as D.W.1. It is a fact that the learned Magistrate did not properly examine the accused by bringing to his notice all the circumstances appearing in evidence against him during his examination under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The accused is a highly qualified person. Defective examination of the accused under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is curable under Section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure provided in the facts and circumstances of the case it is found that such examination has not prejudiced him. In all the decisions referred to by the learned Advocate for the respondent it has been shown that accused was prejudiced because of the non-examination or defect in examination under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the instant case, having regard to its the facts, circumstances and the materials on record, we are of the view, that the accused-respondent has not been prejudiced by the slip-shod and insufficient examination under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is a fact a Magistrate or any other Court should observe the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure as far as practicable and must not be careless in complying those provisions. But that does not mean that non-observance of any such provision unless the same has prejudiced the accused resulting in a wrong decision of the Court, it cannot be said that the trial has been vitiated or that conviction and sentence should be set aside. In view of the materials on record, we are of the view, that the learned Magistrate was legally justified in finding the accused-respondent guilty of an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and the decision has been rightly upheld by the Court of appeal below. 

 24. So far as the inadequacy of punishment is concerned, the learned Advocate for the appellant has referred to the decision reported in 42 DLR 171 and also to the decision reported in AIR 1973 (SC) 467. In the case reported in 42 DLR 171 the sentence of two years imprisonment was raised to five years in view of the heinousness of the crime and in the other case the sentence of life imprisonment was converted into death. Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act provides that a person guilty of an offence under this Section may be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to thrice the amount of the cheque, or with both. Be it mentioned that fine at the time of commission of the offence was not thrice but twice the amount of the cheque and by subsequent amendment in 2000 it has been made thrice the amount of the cheque. Therefore, the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that fine may be enhanced to the tune of thrice the amount of the cheque is not permitted by law. 

 25. Issuing of a cheque knowing well that the drawer of the cheque has no fund in the Bank and making no arrangement for honouring the chqeue by the Bank by itself is a fraudulent act bringing it within the mischief of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. When the Bank returns the cheque referring it to the drawer for want of sufficient fund and the matter is brought to the notice of the drawer, a duty is immediately cast upon the author of the cheque to make immediate arrangement for payment of the money covered by the cheque for saving himself from criminal liability. 

 26. It is well settled that quantum of sentence, though to some extent, is discretionary with the Court, it must be commensurate with the gravity of the offence. In the instant case, dishonest intention being apparent on the face of the record, awarding a sentence of fine only without any substantive sentence of imprisonment is wholly unjustified and improper.
